name: Atom: Low-bit Quantization for Efficient and Accurate LLM Serving
authors: Zhao, Cai, Zhang, Liu, Zhang, Liao, Yang, Yu, Liu, Chen
problem: INT8 weight-activation schemes underuse modern GPUs (which have native 4-bit integer operators), and W4A4 breaks because of block outliers.
mechanism: Mixed-precision block-outlier scheme with fine-grained group quantization: weights are grouped into small blocks and each block's outliers are captured by separate higher-precision channels, with per-group scales; activations get a dedicated outlier path. The design is explicitly aimed at the batched serving regime rather than single-sequence decode, and ships INT4 GEMM kernels that the authors implemented for it.
speedup_reported: Paper's own claim (abstract): 4-bit weight-activation quantization improving END-TO-END serving throughput by up to 7.7x vs FP16 and 2.5x vs INT8 quantization, at the SAME latency target. COMPRESSION RATIO: 4-bit weights + activations (~16x combined vs FP16's 2x16bit). QUALITY COST: described as 'negligible accuracy loss' with no paired number in the abstract. The testbed is an A800 GPU; the speedup is a throughput-at-fixed-latency serving number, which is a much stricter claim than a decode tok/s figure.
